fatal_errors: The cited NbMoTaWVTi study does not demonstrate a dual-BCC bulk product after SPS: it reports two BCC solutions only in milled powder, followed by formation of an FCC TiO precipitate during consolidation.
The cited mechanical properties include precipitation strengthening from TiO, so they cannot substantiate the proposed intermetallic-free, dual-solid-solution strengthening mechanism.
The supplied evidence does not establish a final grain size below 50 nm.

The proposed falsification experiment does not distinguish grain-boundary strengthening from simple solid-solution strengthening because SPS temperature simultaneously changes grain size, phase constitution, contamination, and densification.
explanation: The response addresses the general design problem and selects the same broad processing family—mechanical alloying followed by SPS—with a plausible refractory-alloy alternative. It also invokes grain-boundary and solid-solution strengthening and provides useful temperature and contamination boundaries. However, it does not reconstruct the target CoCrFeNiTi system, its short 1–6 h milling window, 900–1000 °C SPS conditions, or its 83% FCC/17% BCC constitution and measured properties. More importantly, its own strongest evidence contradicts the proposed final microstructure: NbMoTaWVTi has two BCC solutions after milling, but SPS introduces FCC TiO, whose precipitation strengthening contributes to the reported 2709 MPa yield strength. Thus, the numerical outcomes cannot be assigned to a clean dual-BCC nanocrystalline solid solution. The experiment should instead hold composition, density, and phase fractions constant while systematically varying grain size, then test for Hall–Petch scaling; alternatively, annealing-induced grain growth with unchanged chemistry and phase constitution could isolate the grain-boundary contribution.
